newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas edges up late, helped by cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas edges up late, helped by cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures edged up slightly late Friday in moderate trade, helped by reports of firmer bidweek and swing cash prices, industry sources said.
By 1420 EDT, May climbed 1.3 cents to $2.135 per million British thermal units, while June was up the same at $2.135. Most other deferreds were steady to 1.8 cents higher.
"We moved up with the cash, but we could see some downside early next month. May is a shoulder month, and unless we get some heat in the South, cash could come off," said one East Coast trader.
Traders said forecasts for mild U.S. weather through early May could put physical prices on the defensive when next month's flows begin on Thursday.
In addition, they said flatter spreads no longer encouraged early injections.
Technical traders pegged important support in June at $2.03 and then along the short-term up trendline in the $2.00 area. Resistance was seen at $2.24 and then in the $2.33 area.

In the cash, Henry Hub swing prices firmed more than five cents to the $2.15-20 level. May gas at the Gulf was up a nickel to the teens. April Midcon gas held relatively steady in the mid-$1.90s, with May on the same pipes up slightly to the mid-to-high $1.90s. April gas in New York gained more than five cents to the mid-$2.40s, while May city gate was up a couple of cents to the mid-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 23,205 Hub contracts traded at 1350 EDT.
On KCBT, May gained six cents to $2.015, while deferreds were mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 4.7 cents to 12.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
